## 1. Content and Understanding (15 points)

### Depth and Relevance (10 points)
- Demonstrates a strong understanding of the topic by clearly connecting human health and environmental issues using multidisciplinary perspectives.
- Explains technical pathways accurately and integrates key themes from the course, such as vulnerabilities, environmental determinants, and physiological impacts.

\[
\begin{array}{|l|p{10cm}|}
\hline
\textbf{Score} & \textbf{Criteria} \\
\hline
9-10 & Exceptional understanding and integration of course material; technical pathways are clear and insightful. \\
\hline
7-8 & Solid understanding with good integration, though some minor connections or details could be stronger. \\
\hline
5-6 & Basic understanding with limited connections or inaccuracies in technical explanations. \\
\hline
0-4 & Minimal or no understanding demonstrated; weak or irrelevant connections. \\
\hline
\end{array}
\]

### Call to Action (5 points)
- Includes a clear and actionable message tied directly to the issue.
- The call to action is realistic, impactful, and well-supported by the poster content.

\[
\begin{array}{|l|p{10cm}|}
\hline
\textbf{Score} & \textbf{Criteria} \\
\hline
5 & Highly actionable, relevant, and strongly connected to the issue. \\
\hline
3-4 & Clear and relevant, but could be more specific or impactful. \\
\hline
0-2 & Vague, unrealistic, or missing call to action. \\
\hline
\end{array}
\]

---

## 2. Critical Thinking and Creativity (15 points)

### Originality and Engagement (10 points)
- Uses creative approaches to presenting the issue and engaging the audience.
- Demonstrates critical thinking by analyzing vulnerabilities, systemic challenges, and trade-offs.
- Explores evidence-based solutions or connections to inspire meaningful action.

\[
\begin{array}{|l|p{10cm}|}
\hline
\textbf{Score} & \textbf{Criteria} \\
\hline
9-10 & Exceptionally creative and thoughtful, with deep, nuanced analysis. \\
\hline
7-8 & Strong creativity and analysis, though some aspects could be more polished or in-depth. \\
\hline
5-6 & Somewhat creative or analytical, but largely conventional or surface-level. \\
\hline
0-4 & Minimal creativity or critical thinking; lacks depth. \\
\hline
\end{array}
\]

### Audience Engagement (5 points)
- Tailored to the target audience (public or stakeholders), with clear, accessible language.
- Avoids unnecessary jargon and effectively balances technical details with simplicity.

\[
\begin{array}{|l|p{10cm}|}
\hline
\textbf{Score} & \textbf{Criteria} \\
\hline
5 & Highly engaging and audience-appropriate, balancing complexity and clarity. \\
\hline
3-4 & Clear and relevant, though engagement could be stronger. \\
\hline
0-2 & Ineffective or inaccessible to the intended audience. \\
\hline
\end{array}
\]

---

## 3. Design and Impact (10 points)

### Visual Appeal and Organization (5 points)
- The poster is visually engaging, with a professional and cohesive layout.
- Graphics, colors, and text are well-chosen to enhance readability and understanding.

\[
\begin{array}{|l|p{10cm}|}
\hline
\textbf{Score} & \textbf{Criteria} \\
\hline
5 & Outstanding design that enhances the message. \\
\hline
3-4 & Solid design, with minor areas for improvement in layout or visuals. \\
\hline
0-2 & Poor design; visuals detract from content. \\
\hline
\end{array}
\]

### Overall Impact (5 points)
- Does the poster leave a lasting impression and inspire action?
- Aligns with the assignment’s goals by effectively linking human health and the environment.

\[
\begin{array}{|l|p{10cm}|}
\hline
\textbf{Score} & \textbf{Criteria} \\
\hline
5 & Highly impactful and aligned with the assignment’s goals. \\
\hline
3-4 & Somewhat impactful but could be more memorable or inspiring. \\
\hline
0-2 & Minimal impact or alignment with goals. \\
\hline
\end{array}
\]
